newsitem.title: USA: Reno says no pressure applied in Olympic bombing.
newsitem.headline: Reno says no pressure applied in Olympic bombing.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno said Thursday top Justice Department officials never put pressure on investigators to solve the Olympics bombing before the Games ended.

"I've never heard anything like that," Reno said when asked about allegations that investigators in Atlanta felt pressured by officials in Washington for a fast arrest after the July 27 bombing that caused two deaths and injured 111.
"What I've learned long ago is you cannot tell when an investigation will be concluded," Reno said at her weekly Justice Department news conference.
Asked about concerns the investigation may have stalled, Reno said the probe continued and vowed it would go on until those responsible had been brought to justice.
She added, "As I have explained to you on other occasions, sometimes a crime doesn't get solved overnight. But it doen't mean that you stop trying."

Richard Jewell, a security guard who found the pipe bomb before it went off, has been the only named suspect in the federal investigation. He has maintained his innocence since first being named as a suspect.
Justice Department officials have said they are investigating other suspects, but refuse to give details.
